family.trigem-sx386.description: 80386SX motherboards that TriGem built in the early 1990s for other companies to fit in their computers.
family.trigem-sx386.history:
SX386 groups the 80386SX motherboards that TriGem built in the early 1990s for other companies. They did not reach shops under the TriGem name: buyers found them inside a computer carrying the integrator's brand.

The best documented is the SX386M, revision KS-II. It has a 16 MHz 80386SX with an 8 MHz low-speed mode, a socket for an 80387SX coprocessor, up to 8 MB of parity memory, floppy and IDE controllers, two serial ports, one parallel port and six ISA slots, four of them 16-bit; video was on a separate card. Its chipset is the Headland HT101SX, HT113 and GC102-PC trio, the same as in the Olivetti PCS 386SX, but sharing a chipset does not make it an Olivetti design. The BIOS is by AMI, dated February 1991.

The board is known inside the Emerson Elite SX386/16, made in Korea, and the CMS Enhancements ESP SX386M, from the period when CMS and TriGem joined forces to sell CMS-branded computers. A motherboard catalogue also associates it with the Epson CW3S16, although no Epson board has been compared. An Epson guide also describes the SX386MC of the CW3S20/C, at 20 MHz, with 32 KB of cache and up to 32 MB of memory: it is another revision of the same line, not the same board.
